about.title: Highland Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Highland's crash reports show a steady pattern: collisions cluster on Saturday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., often along Baseline Street, Victoria Avenue, SR-210, and 9th Street. With 154 injury collisions and 241 people injured in the most recent final year, and 6 lives lost, the toll on local families is real. If you were hurt in one of these crashes, the period right after matters. Photos, witness names, and vehicle damage can disappear or get overlooked quickly, and the other driver's insurer may call asking for a recorded statement before you've even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't practice law and doesn't promise outcomes — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney familiar with San Bernardino County claims who can help you understand your options before you say anything to an insurance company.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Most After a Highland Car Accident

items.title: California's Two-Year Clock
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, though claims against a government entity — such as for a road defect — can require notice in as little as six months. An independent attorney can help you track which deadline applies to your situation.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for the collision, with your share of fault reducing the amount rather than eliminating it. This matters on multi-vehicle corridors like SR-210 where fault can be disputed.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses in a standard car accident claim, unlike some medical malpractice cases. Because these values aren't fixed by law, having someone evaluate your claim independently can matter.

items.question: Should I give the other driver's insurance company a recorded statement?
items.answer: It's generally wise to avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer before speaking with an attorney. Adjusters are trained to ask questions that can be used to minimize your claim later. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Are crashes worse at certain times in Highland?
items.answer: Public crash records show Highland's reported collisions tend to peak on Saturdays between 3 and 5 p.m., with Baseline Street, Victoria Avenue, SR-210, and 9th Street among the higher-volume corridors by collision count. These are neutral public records, not a judgment about any particular road or driver.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free connection service, and attorneys in our network typically work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless they recover compensation for you. There's no obligation to move forward after you speak with one.
